Affirmations	
119
Practitioner: What’s another time that you made a goal and went 
for it? [open-ended question]
In the previous dialogue, the client starts to voice change talk. The 
practitioner follows with an affirmation to help solidify her commitment. 
The client then makes a powerful strengths-based statement about herself. 
The practitioner can strategically use that statement as a springboard to 
elicit more positive statements. It can also be used in future dialogues to 
help further cement her commitment to change.
There’s never a bad time or place for an affirmation. Always be on 
the lookout for a characteristic or attribute to affirm. Including affirma-
tions in the mix with open-ended questions, reflections and summaries will 
increase your client’s confidence in behavior change.
